In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effective low-energy supergravity lagrangian for orbifold compactifications of superstrings is given by the tree level classical lagrangian plus the one-loop modular-invariant counterterm plus the supersymmetric completion of the classical lagrangian, i.e. all terms consistent with supersymmetry.
the effective low-energy field theories of string compactification beyond the classical approximation have a well defined ultraviolet behaviour and are free from the problems of modular invariance.

, in the absence of supersymmetry, the effective theory of superstring compactification is nonrenormalizable, in the sense that there are no consistent ultraviolet cutoffs for the effective theory, while, if supersymmetry is present, the theory is renormalizable, in that there are consistent cutoffs.

we have shown that the effective low-energy lagrangians for orbifold compactifications are consistent with supersymmetry, modular invariance and the correct ultraviolet behaviour.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the cut-off scale for the effective theory of supergravity is the Planck mass.
the axion couplings in the low-energy effective field theory are determined by the underlying string theory and cannot be chosen arbitrarily.
the effective theory for superstring orbifold compactifications has an ultraviolet cut-off that is the string scale and is independent of the compactification scale.
